entry.title: Merge tag '9p-for-7.4-rc2' of https://github.com/martinetd/linux
entry.content:
Merge tag '9p-for-7.4-rc2' of https://github.com/martinetd/linux

Pull late 9p updates from Dominique Martinet:
 "This is mostly a huge wave of LLM-driven fixes. At least the LLM fixes
  sort of slowed down recently? Or maybe it's just the time of the cycle
  and/or I got used to it, time will tell...

  A few exceptions:

   - a new vsock transport was added, since it's a variant of the
     existing fd/tcp transport there is little harm in taking it in

   - there's an incomplete fix for when file actual size doesn't match
     the size attribute (e.g. exports of sysfs).

     The fix addresses when st_size > actual size with cache=none but
     just about everything else is still broken (st_size=0 with actual
     data regardless of cache, or with data cache st_size > actual is
     still wrong and so are symlinks with 0 size)...

     Maybe at some point I'll find time to understand how netfs works
     and address these :|

   - some fixes for the usbg transport by its author, thank you!"

entry.title: vfs: fix take_dentry_name_snapshot() semantics
entry.content:
vfs: fix take_dentry_name_snapshot() semantics

The take_dentry_name_snapshot() function would keep trying to take a
reference on a dentry name forever, even if that dentry had been
released and the dentry name would never become valid.

All normal users held a reference to the dentry, but this "dentry name
is dead" could hit the overlayfs RCU walk case, and Amir fixed it by
adding a new try_take_dentry_name_snapshot() that returns on failure.
See commit 15c6bd5cf109 ("vfs: add try_take_dentry_name_snapshot()").

However, that fix was uncomfortably ugly, and the new "try" version was
subtly buggy in that it would also fail spuriously during a rename. The
only current user of that doesn't really care: a spurious failure would
result in the lookup just exiting RCU mode and being retried with the
dentry ref held (using the non-try version), but this all just rubbed me
the wrong way.

Instead of introducing a new and differently buggy helper, this just
makes take_dentry_name_snapshot() deal with all these situations
correctly.

It does that by instead of retrying when the external name reference
cannot be taken, it now retries purely based on the dentry sequence
counter. That means that if the external name reference failed due to a
rename, we will correctly retry it, but if it fails because the dentry
is dead and the name really is gone, it will now return that failure
rather than looping forever.

In this model, take_dentry_name_snapshot() will never return a failure
when a dentry ref is held, so the existing non-overlayfs users don't
need to care and they can safely ignore the return value.

And users that don't hold a reference (ie currently only that overlayfs
case) can use the improved take_dentry_name_snapshot() function safely
and it won't loop forever when racing with the dentry being free'd.

To make this all really robust and easy to use for any possible new use
cases, the failure case will not just return false, but also make sure
that the returned name will be empty, and that you can still call
release_dentry_name_snapshot() on the name.

But since there won't actually be anything to release on failure, you
can also do what overlayfs does: return an error and *not* call the
release function.

IOW, instead of two different functions that each had their own problem
cases, we're now back to just one single function that is robust and
easy to use in all situations. Knock wood.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/CAHk-=wiPhTLn1p0ZHx-7SMdk4_zazqDK1k7MMEn9scRfqeDgtw@mail.gmail.com/
Fixes: 15c6bd5cf109 ("vfs: add try_take_dentry_name_snapshot()")

entry.title: Merge tag 'bpf-fixes' of git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/gi…
entry.content:
Merge tag 'bpf-fixes' of git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/bpf/bpf

Pull bpf fixes from Alexei Starovoitov:
 "Fix various bugs in bpf core and bpf-lwt. Looks like the speed of us
  fixing bugs is higher than the number of new bugs found. Not out of
  the woods yet. sockmap fixes will come later.

   - Various fixes (Alexei Starovoitov):
       - Use one may_goto time slice per prog invocation instead of one
         per stack frame to fix a soft lockup in loops that nest across
         calls
       - Fix use-after-free in btf__add_type() in libbpf
       - Invalidate a dynptr slice when its stack buffer is written or
         when the frame of the buffer returns
       - Fix the tracking of pointers to the stack in SCEV
       - Keep the valid bytes of a packet pointer in SCEV
       - Fix bpf_throw() in a prog with a private stack in x86 JIT
       - Compare the arguments of an extension prog with those of its
         target
       - Don't accept memory of the prog for struct arguments of
         KF_ACQUIRE kfuncs and for arguments of an empty struct type
       - Fix mmap() of an arena: refuse address 0 and a length above
         max_entries pages, etc.
       - Don't let bpf_skb_adjust_room() raise gso_size to GSO_BY_FRAGS
       - Fix lwt progs: reset skb->cb and don't leave a stale MAC header
         after a prog pushes an IP header, require BPF_LWT_REROUTE when
         an lwt_in prog changes the protocol, don't call into IPv6 when
         it is disabled, don't look for the SRH again in the End.BPF
         helpers, and set a dst for test runs of lwt_in progs

   - Fix bpf_dynptr_copy() for overlapping ranges in one packet
     (Ayushman Rout)

   - Various fixes (Chris Mason):
       - Reject memory of the prog for kfunc projection type arguments
       - Require prog fd or capability for cgroup prog detach
       - Keep the skb network offset signed in cgroup skb progs
       - Reject non-IPv6 packets in BPF_LWT_ENCAP_SEG6
       - Limit the SRH length and move the MAC header in
         bpf_lwt_seg6_adjust_srh()
       - Move the transport header together with the headers that
         bpf_skb_adjust_room() and bpf_lwt_seg6_adjust_srh() move, and
         use the inner transport header after a decap
       - Check the offset in bpf_skb_generic_{push,pop}()

   - Mark jmp mode of ftrace direct trampolines on x86 by clearing bit
     63 of the address instead of setting bit 0, since an ftrace
     callback can start at an odd address (Daniel Borkmann)

   - Fix psock update-side data races on sk->sk_prot and progs in
     sockmap (Jakub Sitnicki)

   - Fix skb_pull() BUG in __bpf_redirect_neigh(): make sure that the
     MAC and IP headers are there and are linear (Jamal Hadi Salim)

   - Fix jited line info that is off by the CFI preamble on x86-64,
     arm64 and riscv64 (Jose Fernandez)

   - Clamp the trace length in __bpf_get_stack() to fix a write after
     the end of the buffer (Josef Bacik)

   - Drop percpu_counter from the htab element count, since its lock can
     deadlock with NMI and tracing progs that update the same map
     (Puranjay Mohan)

   - Propagate scalar precision through stack arguments (Xu Yunxiang)

   - Fix callback recursion selftest with llvm24 (Yonghong Song)

   - Free the skb when bpf_xmit() fails to expand the headroom (Yuqiang
     Sun)"

entry.title: libbpf: Fix use-after-free in btf__add_type
entry.content:
libbpf: Fix use-after-free in btf__add_type

For every string btf_rewrite_str() does:

  off = btf__add_str(p->dst, btf__str_by_offset(p->src, *str_off));

When the string belongs to the base, the pointer goes into the raw data
of the base. btf__add_str() looks the string up in the base first,
btf__find_str() calls btf_ensure_modifiable() on the base, and that
frees the raw data. Then strset__find_str() reads the freed string.

Make all the bases of dst modifiable before the pointer is taken.

This bug is triggered by the sharing of BTF bases between src
and dst, as introduced by the resolve_btfids changes to build
inline BTF.

Fixes: cf91a7db92c6 ("resolve_btfids: Build separate main and inline BTF objects")
Reported-by: Nathan Chancellor <nathan@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>

entry.title: Merge branch 'bpf-fix-stack-argument-precision-propagation'
entry.content:
Merge branch 'bpf-fix-stack-argument-precision-propagation'

Xu Yunxiang says:

====================
bpf: Fix stack argument precision propagation

Outgoing stack arguments retain scalar state separately from registers
and ordinary spills. Their precision dependencies must reach ancestor
states when verification reuses a state or falls back to marking all
scalars precise. Otherwise, an out-of-bounds map access can reuse a state
validated for an in-bounds argument.

Patch 1 covers outgoing scalar argument slots in both precision paths.
Patch 2 adds two load-only asm regressions in verifier_stack_arg.c, based
on Alexei's examples.

Changes in v2:
- Keep the patch 1 fix and explanation unchanged; rebase onto bpf/master
  at 03b013897454064e0a2d84a8ba9a24753eb02f2b.
- Replace the standalone instruction/BTF test builder with two asm tests
  in the existing verifier_stack_arg.c, as requested by Alexei.
- Reuse that file's compiler capability and architecture guards, which
  already cover x86-64, arm64 and RV64. Drop the separate host-side guard.
- Rewrite patch 2's explanation for the two replacement tests.

v1:
https://lore.kernel.org/bpf/20261027061303.1754535-1-xyx2021@mail.ustc.edu.cn/
Review:
https://lore.kernel.org/bpf/DMJI3GWXQOC9.UA3K9X139AR@gmail.com/

Validation on x86-64 with Clang 23.1.4, JIT enabled and panic_on_warn=1:
- Built all four kernel variants and their BPF test modules, plus the
  complete test_progs runner with BPF_STRICT_BUILD=1.
- The two new tests distinguish the two precision paths:

                         State reuse       Fallback
  Unmodified baseline    wrongly accepts   wrongly accepts
  Propagation fix only   rejects           wrongly accepts
  Fallback fix only      wrongly accepts   rejects
  Complete fix           rejects           rejects

  Rejections report the intended map-value bounds violation. The two
  corresponding in-bounds controls load successfully on all four kernels.
  These programs are never attached or executed.
- All 274 subtests passed, with no skips, across verifier_precision,
  verifier_spill_fill, verifier_subprog_precision, verifier_scalar_ids,
  stack_arg_precision, verifier_stack_arg, verifier_stack_arg_order and
  iters on the complete candidate. No kernel WARN/Oops or panic occurred.
- Compiled the test object under x86-64, arm64 and RV64 guard definitions;
  Clang 20 correctly selects the existing unsupported-compiler dummy.
  Runtime testing was x86-64 only, and the unfiltered suite was not run.

Codex assisted with implementation, test integration, commit messages
and validation. The v2 test code was supplied by Alexei and is used
unchanged.
====================

Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20261102190350.788433-1-xyx2021@mail.ustc.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>

entry.title: selftests/bpf: Exercise stack argument precision on state reuse
entry.content:
selftests/bpf: Exercise stack argument precision on state reuse

Add two asm regressions for the precision of the sixth argument, which
is passed in a stack argument slot and used as a map value offset.

The first test reuses a safe state after storing arg6 from a register.
Precision must propagate from that slot to the register at an earlier
checkpoint, so a later out-of-bounds path cannot reuse that checkpoint.

The second test triggers conservative precision fallback by backtracking
across a store through a register that later becomes a scalar through
pointer subtraction. The caller's argument slot must become precise so
an out-of-bounds argument cannot reuse the safe state.

Both programs are load-only rejection tests and use the existing stack
argument compiler and architecture guards.

The two test programs were supplied by Alexei Starovoitov during review
and are included unchanged.

AI assistance was used in preparing this patch.

Suggested-by: Alexei Starovoitov <alexei.starovoitov@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Xu Yunxiang <xyx2021@mail.ustc.edu.cn>

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/bpf/DMJI3GWXQOC9.UA3K9X139AR@gmail.com/

entry.title: bpf: Propagate scalar precision through stack arguments
entry.content:
bpf: Propagate scalar precision through stack arguments

Outgoing stack arguments retain scalar verifier state separately from
registers and ordinary spills. State comparison uses their precision
marks, but propagate_precision() does not carry those dependencies from
a reused state to the current path's ancestors. A path can consequently
reuse a state without making earlier checkpoints distinguish scalar
values that will later be used as memory offsets.

Seed the existing backtracking batch with precise scalar argument slots
from every frame. Incoming arguments live in the caller's outgoing
slots, so include caller frames as well as the current frame.

Also cover scalar argument slots in bpf_mark_all_scalars_precise(), so
conservative fallback preserves the same invariant. Keep its existing
ancestor-only traversal and leave pointer and uninitialized slots alone.

AI assistance was used in preparing this patch.

Fixes: 0f6bd5e7a804 ("bpf: Support stack arguments for bpf functions")
Signed-off-by: Xu Yunxiang <xyx2021@mail.ustc.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20261102190350.788433-2-xyx2021@mail.ustc.edu.cn
